title: How to not burn much tokens?
author: irshadtriton
selftext:
I'm trying to build a Aviation Economy game, however every 20-30 minutes all the tokens are burned! (ChatGPT Astra Light + Godot). Im not a programmer, but i have a vision for MVP not sure how to get it live without burning much token. 

am i doing something wrong or is it expected to burn all  5 hour limit in 20-30 minutes? How to be efficient here?

comments.author: gamedevjp
comments.body:
Well what subscription do you have? If you’re using anything but the $100 one you’re going to burn them tokens using astra. You need to start knowing when to use which models. 

For me, if I am doing anything large that requires /goal, like prototyping an entire section or generating any art or animation I use Astra Light/Med, for mid level coding stuff I’ll swap to Terra Light/mid and anything stupid simple I either do myself or ask Sol Light. I have a couple different buckets of chats for each of these going. I still burn through my tokens on about day 5 or 6 but I’m in a super experimental phase.

Hope this helps!

replies.author: irshadtriton
replies.body:
This is my first game, so I’m still trying to learn how it works! I’m currently on the $20 plan, but I don't mind upgrading if I see this working. I want to spend more time learning about the development process before upgrading.

I created a game design document and then made a folder under the project 'ReachSky,' feeding the design document into it to develop the entire game. I was hoping to see how it might look, and surprisingly, it did way more than I expected! Now that I have a very basic version, I'm focusing on individual features.

Would you suggest creating more folders under the project, with each folder focusing on one feature? I’m still trying to figure out when to use ASTRA versus a lower AI model. How should I build the sequence or structure? Also, I’m very interested in this whole concept of AI game development any guides or courses you could recommend would be appreciated!

replies.author: gamedevjp
replies.body:
If you want to learn more about the development process before upgrading, then you need to drastically downgrade your model from Astra until you’re ready or you’re going to keep crushing your tokens. Use an older model like GPT 5.5

It’s not about creating more folders, it’s about directing your agent where to look to provide a context whenever you give it a task. For example, if you’re gonna make art with it using the image gen tool, you should have an art instructions file that goes to. If you’re gonna have it write code with best practices, it should read a best practices instruction file first. Make sense? You can even go further to having specific agents do specific tasks for you (art agent, coding agent, document creation agent, etc).

Watching this video

https://youtu.be/dZ8P7zevuGw?is=x4VNsxTnwGZhCC6H

replies.author: stream_of_thought1
replies.body:
In that case you can either budget 1k for tokens for the next 12months, or get a GPU.
I'm running on the 20 plan with gpt doing the planning and troubleshooting, astra for some important fixes, and all the coding locally

replies.author: Hot-Middle7260
replies.body:
At this point, since you’re starting out my absolute recommendation is to ask Terra or Luna to TEACH you the basics. And experiment yourself. It’s slower, but you’ll gain permanent knowledge. 

Working with Astra to make games on $200 plan right now is not efficient. At least not for beginners. I’ve wasted my 20x usage in two days. Let alone 5x, or the $20 plan below that

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Anything below 100$ you don't even have to start. 
I'm on 200$ and constantly out of tokens

replies.author: MildlyConcernedMan91
replies.body: I'm on the 250$/month plan and I also burn through it in a single day so I don't know what to tell you. Try to learn to code? I use it to analyze dopamine release over time based on regression tests of the difficulty. I basically use chatgpt as a QA team.

comments.body: Honestly I think it's a very reasonable expectation to develop a game on a 20 dollar budget

replies.author: Gigaslavx
replies.body: Agreed 2400 in 10 years or like 50 cents per day, I guess it depends how long you need to create an aaa game

comments.author: shlaifu
comments.body: you can greatly speed generation up by being very precise in your prompts on HOW you want systms to be built. The closer you can get to basically the LLM just typing the syntax down for you, the less it will spend on thinking, and the cheaper and faster it gets. And also, much better results because by god these things write bloat....

comments.author: Amiya_desi
comments.body: Using a SOTA model like this for planning is basically sufficient; for the actual implementation, I just use Luna Max directly.

comments.author: klas-klattermus
comments.body: Don't use astra. I'm sure you saw the sales pitch that astra will build your dream game in a weekend but it's like you are potting a tomato plant and worrying that the excavator that you used to fill the pot with soil consumes too much fuel.

comments.author: Beskull
comments.body:
Yeah, you need to get the 100-200/mo subscription to get any real power out of the AI models.

Those plans are a steal btw... They are heavily subsidized ... So it is the right way to get started. 

OR
look at open Code

Hey the latest Chinese model, glm, DeepSeek, etc. They are cheaper, but they are all tokens all the way.

replies.author: KitchenPoltergeist
replies.body:
I agree with this. You can do it on a 20/mo plan but it will take a lot longer. You do need Astra for planning AND code review because the other models make more mistakes and I would honestly stay away from Luna or Terra. They'll confidently build the wrong thing and then later you're burning more tokens just to revert and try again.

I repeat, do not let any of your agents check things into git without having Astra review the code first.
